_what: The twelve bosses that keep a kill count, and how the count is kept. Written before any config was edited. tools/boss_battery.py reads this file, so a name or a number changed here without the configs changing goes red, and the other way round.
_which_twelve: MEASURED, not recalled. Every attackable npc in the tree was listed by its own vislevel; 256 sit at 100 or above, and the twelve below are what is left once the slayer superiors (their own system), the fight cave's lesser waves and the ordinary high-level monsters are set aside. They are the twelve things in this build with a boss's own script, drop table or arena.
_display_names: Each one's name= comes out of its own .npc record rather than being typed here, so the window cannot disagree with what the player sees over the monster's head. King black dragon's lower-case 'black' is the cache's own.

how_a_kill_is_counted._hook: The one funnel every death passes through - the same place ~barrows_potential and ~check_progress_task already hang off, and the reason the Barrows reward potential went there: a second [ai_queue3] on an npc that already has one is a hard build error, so a per-boss hook does not exist for eight of these twelve.
how_a_kill_is_counted._credit: The same test every drop table in this tree opens with - 'if (npc_findhero = ^false) { return; }' - so a kill counts for exactly the player the loot went to. %npc_aggressive_player is the LAST attacker and is not the same thing; ~barrows_potential uses findhero for the same reason.
how_a_kill_is_counted._split_kills: Slayer splits a task kill when the hero and the last attacker differ (check_progress_task does it deliberately, with a comment). A kill count is not split here: one death is one kill, credited to the hero, because two players each being told they killed the same boss is a wrong number rather than a generous one.
how_a_kill_is_counted._varp_write_is_inline: A perm varp can be written straight from npc_death after findhero - ~barrows_potential does exactly that with %barrows_killed_monster. Only the MESSAGE needs a queue, because mes() wants the player context that an npc-context death does not have.
how_a_kill_is_counted.no_runtime_varp_index: This engine cannot pick a varp at runtime: engine.rs2 has no varp commands and no enum outputs one. So the increment and the read are each a GENERATED switch_int over twelve cases, and the two enums do the rest - npc -> index, and index -> name.

where_it_is_shown._window: Its own window, Corey's choice when asked. The quest list was the other option and was not taken: it is a quest list, and twelve rows would push the quests up its scroll.
where_it_is_shown._opened_from: One text row appended to questlist.if's scrolling layer, with an [if_button,questlist:boss_kills] behind it - the same idiom every quest row already uses to open its journal. Discoverable without a new tab, and one component rather than a new opener to design.

bosses.name: Kalphite Queen
bosses._note: The SECOND form. kalphite_queen is the first, and it does not die - the drop table is hooked on the flying form for the same reason, with a comment saying so in drop_tables/scripts/kalphite_queen.rs2. Counting the first form would count every kill twice.
